- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% for next 7–14 days.  
- Model consistently underreacts to sharp price drops; if true outcome drops >5% from prior day, forecast should be adjusted down by 1–3% to match.  
- Model overreacts to short-term spikes; if forecast peaks >10% above recent mean, reduce by 5–10% for next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (alternating +/–), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of smoothing to forecast curve.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses mean reversion; if recent 7-day average is >10% above 30-day average, forecast should trend downward.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5), model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
